Volatility and Risk Assessment

Drawdown Analysis

Maximum Drawdown: The largest peak-to-trough decline was -68.5%. This occurred during the period when Nike reached its all-time low of $2.47 on 2000-02-25. Investors holding through this period experienced significant paper losses but would have recovered if maintaining positions.

Key Takeaways and Investment Implications

  • Strong Long-Term Compounding: Nike delivered a 1282.3% cumulative return over 26 years, translating to a 10.60% CAGR — significantly exceeding inflation and many comparable investments.
  • Decade-Level Performance Variance: The 2010s were exceptional (+604.4%), while the 2000s delivered solid returns (+200.0%) despite including the dot-com bust. The 2020s (to date) show a -34.4% correction from ATH.
  • Drawdown Risk: The maximum drawdown of -68.5% underscores that investors must be prepared for significant volatility. However, recovery was achievable for those maintaining positions.
  • Volatility Regime Shifts: Volatility varied significantly — from ~20% in bull markets to over 40% during crisis periods. Investors should calibrate position sizing accordingly.
  • Volume as Sentiment Indicator: Volume spikes often aligned with major price movements, serving as potential early warning signals of sentiment shifts.
  • ATH as Resistance: The 2021-11-05 ATH of $166.25 represents a significant resistance level. Current prices (61.81) remain ~63% below this peak.
